discovery: Electromagnetically induced transparency and the coherent control of light propagation (slow and stopped light)
subfield: Quantum optics / atomic, molecular and optical physics
motivation: Harris and Imamoglu showed theoretically, and with Boller in 1991 experimentally, that quantum interference between excitation pathways in a laser-driven three-level atom can make an opaque medium transparent while greatly enhancing its dispersion. Electromagnetically induced transparency made atomic coherence a practical tool: one control field could switch absorption, refraction and nonlinearity on and off. Hau's 1999 demonstration of light slowed to 17 m/s in an ultracold atomic gas, and her later stopping, storing and reviving of optical pulses, showed how far this tool could go. EIT now underlies quantum memories for photons, few-photon nonlinear optics, Rydberg-atom quantum optics, precision magnetometry and atomic clocks, and its ideas have carried over to metamaterials and optomechanics. It is a clean, physically transparent idea that changed how we engineer light–matter interaction, and it has been verified in many systems.
